key_insight: Rear-jet blockage encloses a recirculation zone that enhances momentum exchange through larger mixing scales, diluting the front jet while the shielded rear jet rises higher.
engineering_relevance: Tandem-jet designs should account for gap-driven momentum loss rather than assume that each jet follows an isolated-jet trajectory.
method: 40 kHz time-resolved PIV across nine spacing–velocity-ratio conditions.
DMD and SPOD analysis of unsteady shear-layer dynamics.
evidence_signal: Across 68 twin-jet cases and 11 single-jet records, front-jet near-field segments were up to 40% shorter, while gap exchange reached 2.8× the single-jet leeward-zone area-integrated value at r ≈ 7.
watch_item: The mechanism is supported observationally; no growing mode was detected only within the resolvable frequency band and available record length.
paper_title: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics
